land.text: the Chechen half of the Checheno-Ingush ASSR

predecessors.note: 'After the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, the Checheno-Ingush ASSR split into two parts'; Chechnya and Ingushetia separated on 4 June 1992. The RSFSR dossier ends in December 1991.

land.text: Chechnya under Russian direct rule from May 2000; the Chechen Republic as a federal subject of Russia

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps a separate Chechen Republic row to 2005 and removes Chechnya from its Russian row in 2000-2005; the Russian Federation dossier should hold it from 2000.

capitals.name: Grozny
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Grozny (named Dzhokhar-Gala from 1997–2000)'. Taken by Russian forces on 2 February 2000.

rulers.name: Aslan Maskhadov
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Elected January 1997 (Chechnya page); the infobox also gives 1998 for his term; killed 8 March 2005.

correction.text: the Chechen half of the former Checheno-Ingush ASSR around Grozny, the shape of Cliopatria's 1992 row, from Dudayev's declaration of independence on 1 November 1991

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first row is 1992, but the page dates the declaration to 1 November 1991. Chechnya and Ingushetia 'separated on 4 June 1992', so for the first months the Ingush half was still formally joined; it is not drawn.

17,433 km2 against 15,300 km2 (Ichkeria infobox), 16,165 km2 (Chechnya infobox; its lead says 16,500 and its borders section 17,300): ratios 1.14 and 1.08, within the pages' own spread. The shape holds as the claimed territory through 1995 but from 11 December 1994 it is contested (ledger) and 'Russian forces conquered most of the republic' between January and May 1995 (First Chechen War page); the ledger draws that as contest, not as a new shape.

correction.text: all of Chechnya as in Cliopatria's 1992-1995 row: 'complete withdrawal of Russian troops and the preservation of Chechnya's de facto independence' after the Khasavyurt Accord

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the gap in Cliopatria's rows (1996-1999): Cliopatria gives no Chechen shape and its Russian Federation row includes Chechnya in those years (16,926,240 km2 against 16,908,853 km2 in 1992-95). The First Chechen War page says the war ended with Russian troops withdrawn and 'de facto independence' kept; the Chechnya page: 'although de jure it remained a part of Russia'. The eu-22 Russian Federation dossier should leave Chechnya out of 1996-1999.

correction.text: unchanged shape for 2000 only, as the land is contested and then Russian-ruled; from 2001 the land belongs to the Russian Federation (Chechen Republic as a federal subject, 'Chechnya reincorporated into Russia')

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps a separate Chechen Republic for 2000-2005 (and excludes Chechnya from its Russian row, 16,908,807 km2). The pages say Russia seized Grozny on 2 February 2000 and 'established direct rule over Chechnya in May 2000' (the Chechnya page: 'After the re-capture of Grozny in February 2000, the Ichkerian regime fell apart'; the Ichkeria infobox: 'Independent state (de facto; 1991–2000)', government in exile from 2000). So the state ends in 2000 and 2001-2005 is Russian land; 2005 matches only the killing of Maskhadov on 8 March 2005. 17,433 km2 against 16,165 km2 (infobox), ratio 1.08.

region.text: the Chechen half of the former Checheno-Ingush ASSR around Grozny

ledger.note: 1991: Dudayev declares Chechnya independent. 'Dudayev, in his new position as president, issued a unilateral declaration of independence on 1 November 1991' (the Chechnya page repeats it). Russia never recognised it: 'although de jure it remained a part of Russia'. 'Chechnya and Ingushetia separated on 4 June 1992', so the Ingush half is not part of the shape. The page names Chechnya, not a boundary, so the region is my reading.

region.text: all of Chechnya as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: 11 December 1994: Russia invades. 'On 11 December 1994, approximately 40,000 Russian troops crossed the border into Chechnya.' The Grozny assault of New Year's Eve 1994 'ended in a big Russian defeat', the presidential palace fell on 19 January 1995 and the battle for the south of the city ended on 6 March 1995; the Russian forces 'conquered most of the republic in the conventional campaign' between January and May 1995. The whole shape is contested because the page gives no frontline.

region.text: all of Chechnya as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: 31 August 1996: the Khasavyurt Accord ends the war. 'Lebed began negotiations with Maskhadov, leading to the signing of the Khasavyurt Accord on 31 August 1996.' Chechen forces had retaken Grozny from 6 August ('1,500 Chechen fighters infiltrated Grozny and, within hours, surrounded Russian garrisons') and seized Argun and Gudermes; the accord 'deferred the decision on Chechnya's status until 2001'.

region.text: all of Chechnya, from which the federal forces withdrew

ledger.note: December 1996: the last Russian troops leave. The accord 'stipulated the withdrawal of all federal forces from Chechnya by 31 December 1996', and the war 'concluded with the complete withdrawal of Russian troops and the preservation of Chechnya's de facto independence'. The page gives the deadline, not the day of completion; the Moscow peace treaty of 12 May 1997 (Ichkeria page) followed.

region.text: all of Chechnya as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: 12 October 1999: Russian troops cross the Terek. 'On 12 October 1999, the Russian forces crossed the Terek'; the page says the conflict 'entered a new phase on 1 October 1999', when Putin declared Maskhadov's authority illegitimate; 'On 12 November 1999, the Russian flag was raised over Chechnya's second largest city, Gudermes' and 'by 11 December 1999, Russian troops had encircled Shali'. The Chechen incursion into Dagestan of 7 August 1999 took ground in Russia, not here, and is in wars. The zone is the whole shape because the page gives no frontline; the year is the page's, the extent my reading.

region.text: all of Chechnya as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: May 2000: the organised resistance ends and Russia rules directly. 'The battle ended when the Russian army seized the city on 2 February 2000' (the Ichkeria infobox says the fall of Grozny was on 6 February 2000); after the ambush of 23 April 2000: 'Soon, the Russian forces seized the last populated centres of the organized resistance.' The month is the page's for direct rule, the best date for the end of the contest.

region.text: all of Chechnya, under Russian direct rule

ledger.note: May 2000: Russia takes Chechnya. 'Russia established direct rule over Chechnya in May 2000'; Putin appointed Akhmad Kadyrov interim head of the pro-Moscow government. The Ichkeria page: 'subsequently being forcibly subsumed back under the control of the Russian central government in 2000'; the war's infobox: 'Chechnya reincorporated into Russia'. The land is the Russian Federation's from here; Cliopatria's separate row 2000-2005 is wrong.

2000: the de facto Chechen Republic of Ichkeria ends. The Ichkeria infobox gives 'Independent state (de facto; 1991–2000)' and 'Government-in-exile (2000–present)', with an underground government from May 2000; Maskhadov was killed on 8 March 2005 and Umarov 'abolished the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria' on 31 October 2007 (Chechnya page).

wars.name: First Chechen War

zones.text: Chechnya; Russia 'conquered most of the republic' January to May 1995, Chechen forces retook Grozny from 6 August 1996

wars.outcome: Khasavyurt Accord of 31 August 1996; all federal forces out by 31 December 1996 and Chechnya's 'de facto independence' preserved, status deferred.
wars.note: The page counts 3,826 Russian dead by the General Staff and 30,000-100,000 Chechen civilian deaths; no front line is given, so the whole republic is the zone.

wars.name: Second Chechen War

zones.text: Chechnya, taken by Russia from October 1999 to spring 2000

wars.outcome: Russia crossed the Terek on 12 October 1999, seized Grozny on 2 February 2000 and established direct rule in May 2000; the 'counter-terrorism operation' was declared over on 16 April 2009. The Ichkerian state ended in 2000.
wars.note: Includes the War of Dagestan: 'On 7 August 1999, Shamil Basayev together with Ibn al-Khattab' led up to 2,000 fighters into Dagestan, which Russia held. This dossier's state ends in 2000; later years are the insurgency.

certainty.note: A de facto state with no treaty frontier: the boundary with Ingushetia after 4 June 1992 is not described on the pages and the Russian lines in 1995 and 1999-2000 are not given as fronts. The frontiers with Georgia and Dagestan are the Soviet-era republic lines and are sharp.

notes:
Page budget: the brief allows 1-2 pages for a 2-shape state; four were opened because every Chechen border move (December 1994, August 1996, October 1999, May 2000) is dated only on the war pages: Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, Chechnya, First Chechen War, Second Chechen War.

WHAT THE CLIOPATRIA ROWS ARE: 'Chechen Republic' (Q5187, the Wikipedia title 'Chechnya') has shapes for 1992-1995 and 2000-2005 and none for 1996-1999. The pages read here say the de facto state existed 1991-2000 and that Russia held Chechnya from 2000; so the 1992-1995 shape is right (but contested from December 1994), 1996-1999 is a new keyframe (Cliopatria puts Chechnya in the Russian row, 16,926,240 km2, which is 17,387 km2 more than its 1992-1995 and 2000-2005 Russian rows), and 2000-2005 is Russian land. The 2005 end matches only the killing of Maskhadov on 8 March 2005. The Russian Federation dossier (eu-22) should therefore: leave Chechnya out of 1996-1999 and put it back from 2000 (ledger: gain from this state in May 2000, and a loss/contest pair for 1994-1996 and 1999-2000).

MODEL: the whole shape is the contest zone because no page gives a front line: 11 December 1994 to 31 August 1996 and 12 October 1999 to May 2000; the page only says Russia 'conquered most of the republic' in January to May 1995. No occupation event was written for 1995 for that reason. Georgia is the only other neighbour (the page: 'its only gateway to the outside world that was not controlled by Moscow'); no border event.

NOT SETTLED: the area disagrees inside the Chechnya page (infobox 16,165 km2, lead 16,500, borders section 17,300) and with the Ichkeria infobox (15,300); the dates for the fall of Grozny differ (2 February 2000 on the Second Chechen War page, 6 February 2000 in the Ichkeria infobox); the Ichkeria infobox gives Maskhadov's term as 1997-2000 and elsewhere 1998-2000; direct rule is May 2000 on the Second Chechen War page ('the following month' of a May sentence is ambiguous) and the Chechnya page gives no month. The state's end is set to May 2000. Not opened: the 1991-92 Chechen-Ingush boundary, the Treaty of Federation of 31 March 1992 (the First Chechen War page says Chechnya did not sign), the Caucasus Emirate (Umarov, 2007), which held no mapped land on these pages.

NEEDS NO NEW DOSSIER: Ingushetia is a Russian federal subject (a Russian Federation matter); the Caucasus Emirate declared in October 2007 is not territory on the pages read.

GAZETTEER: Chechnya, Ingush and the Cliopatria shape resolve (Cliopatria 67 cells, admin1 Chechnya 64 cells); no new names.
